title: call.score
description: The last entry of a call: what the judges said about it at hang-up, one row per judge. Written after call.summary, and the entry the log seals on.

CallScore.description: The last entry of a call: what the judges said about it at hang-up, one row per judge. Written after call.summary, and the entry the log seals on.

passed.description: Whether no judge answered broken. A deferred or a skipped judge is an answer nobody gave, never a fault of the call. ABSENT when no judge answered at all, which is not the same as false: read not_judged for why nobody did.

not_judged.description: Why nothing judged this call, when nothing did: the judges are not installed on this box, or the judging itself failed. Absent on every call a judge answered.

judges.description: One row per judge that was run over this call, in the order they were declared.

panel.description: Every judge this call declared, whether or not it answered: a judge that raised is here and absent from judges. Empty when nothing was ever declared, and absent on entries written before this field existed.

judge_calls.description: How many questions judging this call actually put to a model. Zero is the happy path: a policy answers by code.

judge_cost_eur.description: What those questions cost in euros, priced from the judge model's own usage rows. Absent when no usage was reported, never zero.

Judgment.description: One judge's answer about one call: the question it was asked, the word it answered and the sentence that says why.

name.description: The judge's own name, as the judge itself declares it: consent, grounded, register, leakage.

criteria.description: The question this judge answered, as it hangs it on every judgment it makes.

reason.description: The judgment's own reasoning: a policy writes the evidence, a model writes one sentence.

JudgmentEvidence.description: Where in the call's own log a judgment is about. A reader who disagrees with a verdict opens the log at those lines.

items.description: One entry of this call, by its seq.

seqs.description: Every entry the judgment named, in the order it named them. Empty when it named none.

said.description: The words the log carries at the first of those entries that carries any: the caller's own yes, the agent's own sentence.
